name: MET
summary: MET, on chromosome 4, encodes the receptor for hepatocyte growth factor, a signalling protein involved in cell growth, survival and movement during development and repair. In Friesian horses a 14 base-pair frameshift deletion in the first exon (c.1559_1572del, p.Pro392Leufs*3; g.74041982_74041995del on chromosome 4, EquCab3.0), associated with the FH2, FH3 and FH4 haplotypes, is reported as a recessive embryonic lethal (Steensma et al. 2026): matings of two carriers had about 25 per cent lower insemination success, as expected if embryos with two copies are lost. Carriers are normal. Among 8,263 Friesians born 1996-2024, the haplotypes were carried by 14.7 (FH2), 13.7 (FH3) and 8.0 (FH4) per cent of horses; the three overlap, and no share of carriers of the deletion itself was published. Fewer horses with two copies of each haplotype were found than expected (15 of 53, 5 of 45, none of 15); the few seen may be recombinants. Mice without MET die as embryos with placental defects. Nothing is seen in the coat, and no effect on build or performance is established.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: Two working copies. Nothing is wrong and nothing is passed on.

phenotypes.name: MET carrier
phenotypes.description: One copy of the deletion. The horse is normal and nothing shows; half its foals inherit the copy. Two carriers bred together are how an embryo with two copies arises.

phenotypes.name: Embryonic lethal (MET)
phenotypes.description: Two copies of the deletion. The embryo is lost early, so the mating appears not to have taken. This is inferred from the lower insemination success of carrier-to-carrier matings, about 25 per cent.
